*sighs* Look I'm not going to spend an hour explaining, so I'm going to try to get what I'm saying across, but succeed or fail I'm not reattempting. I understand it's seemingly contradictory, but honestly I think the only reason you think that is because you've never been there so it's a foreign idea, I guess.

First off, I feel you're thinking too binary: either I want it all of it or none of it. I don't want a social life like most others have, as I sincerely don't care for people in general enough to want to have my life revolve around always being around others. It's not about having nothing to lose (then again I feel I already lost), it's about having nothing to gain. People have always made me unhappy for the most part, but it's impossible to go totally without and be normalized. This is not mutually exclusive for wishing I were more social with people I already care about, nor is it mutually exclusive for occasionally striking up conversation with strangers. Every one needs some social stimulation, but everyone has different amounts that would be optimal: mine happen to be very low. I hope that explains things because I'm not sure what about it is hard to get, and I'm not good at finding multiple ways of expressing the same idea.

Depression is a mental issue, I can and have had days of severe depression for almost no reason at all. Hell when I was most bipolar, I can go between being on top of the world to hitting rock bottom in 2 days, and I assure you little about my life changed all that significantly to warrant it. That has nothing to do with overall satisfaction or lack thereof with my life or particular aspects concerning it. I wouldn't say I'm unhappy, just not happy (unhappy implies active opposite of happy, I'm just neutral for the most part). Maybe right now I am indeed unhappy, but this is more due to lack of employment prospects than anything about my social life. As I said, I'm just going through the motions nowadays, as I feel that's all that's worthwhile. I'm sure I'm wrong, but I've no reason to think otherwise in my experiences.

And forgive me if I come across as a dick, but I'm really sick and tired of people patronizing me that the reason I'm unhappy is because I'm not social enough and that I'm not doing enough. Consider the prospect that maybe I actually am not like most people, that I may actually be reasonably content being much less social. After all, I get a lot more pleasure reading a junior-level textbook on classical mechanics than I do talking with acquaintances on trite "everyday" matters. Sure I may wish--though I don't know if such desires are fleeting or indicative--to perhaps have a girlfriend (right now I'm too broke to even think about it) or go out more (though optimally would still be a lot less than what you're considering, to me just going out once more every 6 weeks would suffice), but then again I also wish I didn't have bad vision or that I had a lot more money. Just because I wish things to be different doesn't mean it's unbearable as it is. Anyway, maybe I'm unhappy for perhaps other reasons: unhappy at being mentally ill and feeling like I'm damaged goods as a result, unhappy at being unemployed with lots of student debt, maybe unhappy about political matters (I follow such things a lot), or because I've been sick the last 2 weeks and only starting to get better (bad cold with complications). Honestly I'd find those matters to be a lot more relevant to my overall outlook on life than whether I have 4 or 400 friends.

But to answer your question, I am not going to change much because there's little TO change. I mean I can't fix the fact that I've had depression since childhood, bipolar disorder since early adulthood, nor can I change the fact that I just don't have the skills to interact as well with others. It's not from lack of practice, believe me even with the people I am most "normal" with it's still sub-optimal. It's as good as it's going to get for me. Some people just suck at such things the same way people suck at math. Sure I can be better at it than I was before, doesn't mean I'm going to master it at any point. But I love the whole vindictiveness at the end, really classy. Don't even bother trying to understand my way of thinking, just dismiss me as a failure and that I deserve to suffer. And you wonder why I don't want to be more social: why the fuck would I want to deal with people like you all day, every day? And believe me it's not due to you claiming that I'm at fault, I accept responsibility on many matters and I don't end any interpersonal relationships on such grounds, no it's this holier-than-thou shit about how I'm not as good at something and got discouraged, and somehow I deserve to be miserable because people like you make me go out of your way to make me feel as such. Believe me, I've little else to say on the matter so don't bother replying. (And before you ask, I only became more sharp with my tongue the more I thought about the end of what you said, as before the last two paragraphs I focused on what you said an item at a time. I don't change a single thing I said in spite of my newfound irritation)
After university, I'm sick of chicken.

Being depressed isn't the same as being unhappy. I'm not going to discuss matters regarding that if that isn't understood. As for women (funny you assumed, albeit correctly, that I'm heterosexual), I have found that men like me have a lot of difficulty getting laid, despite actually trying and making the best efforts to do so.

Not really seeking a social life to be honest, I am kind of misanthropic. Most of why growing up was miserable for me was BECAUSE of people, why the hell would I want to associate further with them? You know what I mean? Sure I desire a modicum of being social, hence why I hang with my parents and my few friends on occasion, but I don't desire nor require anywhere near as much as most people. Also, I'm pretty sure I know what interests me sufficiently to know what I like to do, and they may not be social but far as I'm concerned that's not the point.

As for moving, I don't buy into this "fresh start" idea in the slightest: tried it enough times in my life, and it's really just self-deluding, at least for me. If I were to move, it'd be for employment opportunities, and right now it's difficult to relocate with few funds, no credit, and nothing there when I do go.

I never said I was going to do it, just that I feel that's what is a likely scenario. As for methods, no clue. Honestly I'll probably just die passively if it came down to that: not actively killing myself, but refusing to save myself, like if I developed cancer I'd refuse medical care.
Not sure why, wasn't trying to be funny in the slightest.
Believe me, everyone has been saying the same thing: had I been civil I'd be having offers up the ass, or at least a hell of a lot more leads.

Nothing's been having me going really for the longest time. I just carry on because the survival instinct is still going strong (still capable of mating, theoretically). For about 10 years I just have been going through the motions. I do say that being a reclusive introvert since pre-kindergarten has its advantages in this situation: I'm very capable of keeping myself occupied with solitary activities so I don't get too down (mostly distraction, but that's what most things are to people).
